newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank has enough funds to support banks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank has enough funds to support banks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) Banking Department will have enough money to support banks' liquidity after the government draws on a recently disbursed IMF loan instalment, a BNB deputy governor said on Tuesday.

"The Banking Department deposit with the Issue Department will decrease to some 530 billion levs after a transfer of the $137 million second tranche from the IMF into the government account," Valentin Tsvetanov told reporters.

The Banking Department, a lender of last resort for local commercial banks under a currency board system can refinance sound banks from its deposit with the Issue Department only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system.
The deposit stood at 792 billion levs on July 31, BNB figures showed.
Tsvetanov said the Banking Department was preparing regulations for extending refinancing to sound banks in case of temporary liquidity shortage.
"Banks now have enough free liquidity and they hardly need refinancing from us," said Tsvetanov.
Under the currency board, a form of an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate regime introduced on July 1, the central bank was banned from lending to the government and banks endangered by insolvency.

On July 29 the International Monetary Fund (IMF) transferred to the BNB the second instalment of 100 million Special Drawing Rights or $137 million under a 14-month $510 million standby accord approved in April. The government has not drawn on the instalment so far.
After the government draws on the instalment it will be entered into the government debt account, a part of the Banking Department assets which amounted to 1.194 trillion levs on July 31.

Bulgaria paid debt principal of 10.6 million Special Drawing Rights to the IMF last month through the Banking Department, Tzvetanov said. He did not specify the payments due to the IMF in August. ($=1,866 Bulgarian Levs) -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
